Each iteration: STAGE 0 triage across all streams -> do the single highest-leverage item -> verify -> commit/push -> REFILL (append >=1 new next-step you discovered). STOP only if truly nothing + refill yielded nothing.
thesis: anvil-engine (self-hosted CDP browser) is shared infra. Relay = consumer text-a-bot on anvil. DataFaucet = dev/MCP layer; its capture flow still pays Browserbase — moving it to anvil unifies the stack and removes the vendor. Synergy: one browser engine, two products, zero browser vendor.

milestones.goal: Graceful degradation under partial failure. Relay has many paths (inbound + scheduler + recipes + digests + alerts) but its behavior when a DEPENDENCY is down (anvil unreachable, LLM 5xx/quota, memory-file unwritable) is only partly tested. Make every path fail soft with a clear user message + a logged reason, never a crash or silent hang, and pin it with tests. Consumer-trust + 24/7-deploy hardening on the WHOLE surface, not just the happy path.
milestones.done_when: anvil-down + LLM-error + unwritable-store degrade to a clear reply (inbound) or a logged skip (proactive) with tests for each; no unhandled rejection can crash the worker; a doc note on the failure modes

milestones.goal: Prove the REAL pipe, not just types. The channel->agent->anvil->reply path is heavily unit-tested (358) but the existing scripts/e2e-*.mjs are offline/stubbed. anvil is reachable locally; build a real live-e2e harness that drives the actual agent + real anvil for the canonical errands (scrape a page, fetch_json an API, multi-step browse) and ASSERTS real output. So the day Alex provisions the VM, the deploy path is verified working, not just green on tsc. Bounded (few LLM calls; skip cleanly when keys/anvil absent so CI stays offline).
milestones.done_when: a `npm run e2e:live` (or scripts/e2e-live.mjs) drives real anvil end-to-end for >=2 canonical errands and asserts real content; skips gracefully (exit 0 + SKIP note) when ANVIL is down or GEMINI_API_KEY absent so offline CI is unaffected; documented in README Verify

milestones.goal: Make the 24/7 deploy OPERABLE from outside the process. Relay tracks metrics + /status internally (Telegram-only), but an operator running it on the VM has no way to SEE health without reading logs or texting the bot. Add an offline-inspectable operability surface: a `relay status` CLI (or npm script) that reads the DURABLE state files (schedules, recipes, digests, alerts, last metrics) + probes anvil, and prints a health summary + counts — no bot, no keys needed for the counts. So the operator can ssh in and run one command to see whats scheduled, whats watched, and whether anvil is up.
milestones.done_when: a `npm run status` (scripts/status.mjs) reads the durable stores + probes anvil and prints a health/counts summary (pending schedules, saved recipes/digests/alerts, anvil up/down, last metrics window if present); runs with NO keys (counts are file-based) and degrades cleanly when a store file is absent; documented in README

milestones.done_when: anvil exposes an operator-legible health/metrics surface (sessions active/max, pool state, uptime) beyond a bare /v1/live, OR a documented crash/degradation gap is closed; change is tested (its vitest) + tsc clean; no behavior regression on the default path

milestones.goal: Prove the degradation paths hold under REAL induced failure, not just unit mocks. m14 made Relay fail soft and unit-tested it with injected throwing deps; but nobody has killed anvil mid-errand against the live stack and confirmed the user gets the friendly line + the worker survives. Build a fault-injection drill harness (CI-safe skip like e2e-live) that induces real faults — anvil unreachable, anvil dies mid-session, a bad/blocked URL — through the REAL agent path and asserts the friendly classification + no crash. Closes the gap between unit-proven and deploy-proven for the failure modes.

milestones.goal: Quantify the thesis with REAL measured numbers, not claims. The whole portfolio argues self-hosted anvil beats a Browserbase/Browserless/Steel vendor — no per-session meter, no quota. But nowhere is that PROVEN with data: what is anvil actual end-to-end latency for the canonical errands, and what would the same volume cost on the vendor? Produce a credible, reproducible one-pager: measure anvil scrape/fetch/browse latency locally (script, real runs), put it against published vendor per-session pricing, and state the honest break-even. Credibility artifact for an AE — reproducible, no hand-waving. anvil is up locally so the latency half is measurable now.
milestones.done_when: a reproducible bench script measures real anvil latency across the canonical errands (>=N runs, p50/p95) + a THESIS.md one-pager states measured latency vs vendor per-session cost with an honest break-even + the caveats (compute is the real cost, not the vendor); numbers are from actual runs, not invented; SKIPs/degrades if anvil is down

milestones.goal: Adversarial audit of the agent tool surface. Relay drives a REAL browser for anyone who texts it — the SSRF url-validator + dangerous-action guard are the blast-radius controls, and they have unit tests but no ADVERSARIAL sweep. Systematically try to bypass them (SSRF: decimal/hex/octal IPs, IPv6, redirect-to-internal, DNS-rebind shapes, embedded creds, non-http protocols; dangerous-action: obfuscated pay/delete/submit labels) and fix any gap found. Consumer-trust + real-user-safety hardening — the highest-value non-gated work left now that the stack is proven.
milestones.done_when: an adversarial test sweep exercises the SSRF guard (isUrlSafe) + the dangerous-action guard (isDangerousAction) against a documented list of bypass shapes; any that get through are FIXED (or documented as accepted with rationale); tests pin every case so a regression cant reopen a hole; tsc + full suite green

Consistency + supply-chain hygiene across the stack.
milestones.done_when: the trailing-dot SSRF fix (+ any redaction fix that applies) is mirrored into mcp-forge url-validator on anvil-migration with tests, test:unit green; a documented check confirms each cross-repo shared lib is identical+parity-guarded OR intentionally-diverged-with-reason; NEVER touch master

milestones.goal: Make the kept-identical contract ENFORCED, not manual. m27 documented (SHARED.md) that url-validator.ts + redact-secrets.ts are copied-and-must-mirror between Relay and DataFaucet with NO automated guard — and the audit found they had actually drifted. anvil-client already has a byte-parity test in both repos; give these two the same treatment so a future edit that forgets to mirror fails CI instead of silently splitting the SSRF/redaction behavior across the two products. milestones.done_when: a parity test in Relay asserts url-validator.ts + redact-secrets.ts match the mcp-forge copies (skips gracefully if ../mcp-forge absent, like anvil-client-parity); if a byte-diff is too strict for the doc-comment differences, the guard normalizes comments OR the files are made truly byte-identical; tsc + suite green; SHARED.md updated to move these from manual to guarded

milestones.goal: Give the agent a real capability it lacks: acting on pages behind a cookie/session. Today Relay can only read PUBLIC pages — anvil sessions start fresh + logged-out, so a user cant say check my <account> because the agent has no way to carry an auth cookie. Add a SAFE, opt-in cookie-passing path: the user (or an env-provided cookie for a specific host) can seed cookies into an anvil session so the agent can read a page the user is entitled to, with the SSRF + dangerous-action guards still enforced and cookies redacted from logs. Real product depth — the #1 thing separating a demo from a useful assistant. anvil already exposes cookie set/get (see ANVIL-CONTRACT /v1/cookies).
milestones.done_when: the agent can be given cookies for a specific host (via a guarded tool or env-seeded per-host cookie jar) that anvil applies to the session before navigating, so it can read an authorized logged-in page; cookies are host-scoped (never sent cross-origin), redacted from all logs/replies, and the dangerous-action guard still blocks state changes; unit-tested offline (mock anvil cookie API); documented incl. the security model in SECURITY.md
